# THE LOUNGE [italic]Cutting, lighting, keeping and the manners of a good cigar, as taught at the first table on the Calle Obispo.[/italic]
## THE CUT Cut the cap, not the cigar. A clean cut a few millimetres from the end is enough. If you have no cutter, a sharp knife will do. Your teeth will not.
## THE LIGHT - [bold]Matches[/bold] are best. Let the sulphur burn off before the flame touches the leaf. - [bold]A lighter[/bold] is acceptable. A petrol lighter will leave a taste. The House forgives you. - [bold]A welding torch[/bold], a flare or the exhaust of a dropship are not acceptable. We have been asked. More than once.
Toast the foot evenly and slowly. Do not hurry. Nothing on a colony ever comes on time, and a cigar should be no exception.
## THE PACE A puff a minute. If the cigar goes out, it is not a failure, it is a pause. Relight it gently.
## KEEPING YOUR CIGARS - Keep them in a closed case, away from the processor vents and the dry air of a ship. - Hypersleep is hard on cigars. Pack them in a sealed travelling case before you go under. - Never keep cigars beside rations, coffee or anything that smells. Leaf drinks in what is near it.
## MANNERS - Ask before you light. On a colony, you share the air, and somebody worked very hard to make it. - Never smoke in a hydroponics bay, a clinic, a cryo ward, an ammunition store or near an oxygen line. - Never let a cigar burn in an ashtray unattended. Colony fires are not like fires on Earth. There is nowhere to run. - Offer one to the person who fixed your air. They will remember.
